stories.text: Licensed in 1929 and opened in 1930 by Sir Sefton Brancker, it was one of Britain's first municipal aerodromes. In the Second World War it repaired Lancaster bombers; its 18 concrete pillboxes are all listed. The airfield closed on 6 June 2025, sold to the Vistry Group to build 4,000 houses.[^village]

315959.sum: The building was built in 1941, according to Historic England (via Wikipedia). It is Grade II listed.

stories.text: St Peter's dates from the end of the 12th century; work in 1909 gave it the shape it has today. It is listed Grade II.

317730.sum: St. Peter's Church is a Grade-II listed church located in Tollerton, Nottinghamshire, England.

stories.text: Tollerton Hall dates from about 1675, or from 1792 by another account, and was much altered in the 18th and 19th centuries, when Gothic Revival towers, turrets and battlements were added.[^s1] After 1929 it was a sports club and hotel.[^s1] In the Second World War it was used for training before D-Day and then as a camp for German and Italian prisoners.[^s1] In 1948 the Roman Catholic Diocese of Nottingham opened St Hugh's College here, a junior seminary for boys from 11; it took other boys from 1969 and closed in 1986.[^s1][^s2] The hall was then a company's headquarters until 2017, when it became a private home again.[^s2] It is listed Grade II.

317731.sum: St Hugh's College was a Roman Catholic minor seminary in Tollerton founded by the Diocese of Nottingham. The manor house dates to 1792, and the college was founded on the premises in 1948. It closed in 1986 and is a Grade II listed building.
